text: President Xi Jinping told the opening of the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai on 17 July that the world needs a just and equitable system for governing AI, and announced a World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organisation with 29 founding member countries plus joint AI application centres to be built with ASEAN, the League of Arab States, the African Union, CELAC, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation and BRICS.

Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn set out the bloc's approach to AI governance at the high-level meeting held alongside that Shanghai conference on 18 July, saying governments, international organisations, industry and universities will all be needed to handle what is coming.

The African Union Commission and Smart Africa agreed in Geneva on 20 July to coordinate delivery of the Continental AI Strategy, with an action plan, a financing plan and AI governance guidelines in preparation, alongside a proposed African Union AI fund and a pan-African AI centre.

Forum ICT ministers met in Port Moresby on 24 July with Papua New Guinea taking the chair, and put artificial intelligence, safer online spaces and how the region measures its own digital progress on the agenda under the Lagatoi Declaration.

The Caribbean Telecommunications Union closed its Caribbean Artificial Intelligence Forum in Trinidad and Tobago on 25 July and released the Caribbean AI Task Force report, which asks CARICOM states to harmonise AI policy and treat data sovereignty as a shared regional asset.

At the UN Expert Mechanism on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples in July, delegates from Sami, Inuit and Ojibwe organisations argued that data centre projects should have to meet the standard of free, prior and informed consent, citing a Chilean environmental tribunal's suspension of a Google site in Santiago and a complaint brought by the Anace people against a data centre in north-east Brazil.

Five coalitions published a joint read-out of the opening session of the UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance on 24 July, reporting that women and Indigenous Peoples were insufficiently represented across the talks and that chances for governments and other stakeholders to speak to each other directly stayed limited.

Two artificial intelligence bills, one in the Senate and one in the Chamber of Representatives, had cleared committee and remained in play as of 16 July, setting out rules for the development and supervision of AI systems with the science ministry to lead implementation.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on 15 July that large data centres will be required to underwrite their own new power supply, pay their share of connection costs and meet water efficiency standards under a mandatory national framework, to be put to national cabinet next month and to parliament early next year.

Governor Kathy Hochul signed an executive order on 15 July halting new state environmental permits for data centres while regulators take up to a year to write rules on energy use, water use and protections for surrounding communities.

Two county council committees voted on 22 July to advance an 18-month pause on new data centres and zoning that would block any facility above 25 megawatts, backed on the record by a coalition of more than 30 community, environmental and faith groups.
A UN News report on the Secretary-General's governance call was mostly about autonomous weapons, so it is not logged here.

The law implementing the EU AI Act in Germany, the KI-MIG, entered into force on 29 July and makes the Bundesnetzagentur the country's market surveillance authority, single contact point and complaints body for artificial intelligence, with direct oversight of systems used in employment, critical infrastructure and education.

The Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment announced on 30 July that the AI Office of Ireland has been established as an independent statutory body under the Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Act signed on 21 July, with Paul Byrne appointed as its first chief executive and the office due to be operational by 2 August.

The European Commission opened bidding on 30 July for up to seven AI gigafactories across the bloc, backed by about 10 billion euros of public money and an expected 30 billion euros in total once private investment is counted, with consortia given until 12 November to apply and awards due in early 2027.

The Ministry of Science and ICT launched an AI data centre alliance on 29 July, co-chaired by the minister and the chief executive of SK Telecom, bringing twelve companies together behind a national target of 18.4 gigawatts of data centre capacity by 2035.

The National AI Office closed its public consultation on a proposed AI Governance Bill on 31 July, after three weeks open from 10 July, on a law that would apply to AI systems placed on the market, developed or used in Malaysia.

Digital and AI ministers from the 21 APEC economies met in Chengdu on 23 July and issued a joint statement backing human-centred and locally tailored AI, voluntary experience sharing and technical assistance, while recording that members take different approaches to their own AI policies.

President José Raúl Mulino launched the National Advanced Technologies Agenda on 30 July, whose AI strategy rests on six pillars including data governance and AI ethics and regulation, and which sits alongside a bill on adaptive governance of artificial intelligence now before the National Assembly.

The Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy opened public participation on 27 July on a draft Artificial Intelligence and Other Emerging Technologies Policy, taking written submissions from institutions, industry, academia, civil society and the public until 4 August.

The government approved a 170 million US dollar project reported on 24 July for a sovereign data centre, a government digital platform and a smart border system, to be delivered with Cisco and Cybastion.

The county quorum court voted 10 to 3 on 28 July against a twelve month pause on data centre construction, and separately rejected by 8 to 6 an amendment that would have required the AVAIO Digital project near Wrightsville to meet any future county rules before its later phases.

County leaders held a standing room only public forum on data centres on 28 July, at which the judge executive said every person present raised a hand against them and reported a survey of 1,500 residents in which 80 per cent said no, ahead of a fiscal court vote on a moratorium set for 11 August.
Dropped as older than it looked: the Future of Life Institute Summer 2026 AI Safety Index was published on 7 July, not in this window.
Dropped as older than it looked: the Cape Town planning tribunal approval of the Equinix hyperscale data centre was 14 July, and no appeal had been filed by the time of this scan.
Dropped as older than it looked: the New Jersey FAIR Act on algorithmic rent setting was enacted on 20 July, outside the window for national and state items.

Dropped as unverified: several secondary summaries said Pacific ICT ministers adopted regional AI principles at Port Moresby, but the Pacific news sources checked only record AI as an agenda item, so it is not logged.

Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, the Digital Omnibus on AI, entered into force on 27 July and amends the AI Act to push stand-alone high-risk obligations from 2 August 2026 back to 2 December 2027 and embedded high-risk systems from 2 August 2027 back to 2 August 2028, while adding two prohibited practices from 2 December 2026 covering AI that generates non-consensual intimate images and child sexual abuse material.

Public comment closed on 31 July on a proposed Federal Trade Commission policy statement on accuracy in AI systems, which argues that state laws appearing to coerce companies into altering the output of their models, naming Colorado's Artificial Intelligence Act, may be impliedly preempted by federal law.
The full county council voted unanimously on 28 July to adopt the 18-month pause on new data centre permits, moving it past the committee stage logged here on 22 July.

The state congress repealed the artificial intelligence provisions of the state penal code on 30 July, striking the chapter on improper use of AI to cause social alarm, and Governor Ricardo Gallardo Cardona said a broader AI law would be drafted this year with academics, health specialists and psychologists.

Dropped as older than it looked: the Ohio Environmental Protection Agency refused a blanket wastewater discharge permit for data centres after about 7,000 opposing public comments, but the decision was reported on 22 July, nine days before this scan.

Dropped as older than it looked: more than 1,200 objections against the 600 megawatt Cato data centre at Auchtertool in Fife were reported on 24 July, outside the 48-hour window that applies to large regulators, though the Fife Council consultation was still open.

Dropped as older than it looked: the Future of Life Institute AI Safety Index for summer 2026 was released around 10 to 14 July, and the West African six-country AI governance framework and the Smart Africa African AI Council were reported on 10 and 21 July, all outside the seven-day regional window.

The European Commission's AI Office and national authorities began enforcing the AI Act on 2 August, and from the same day interactive AI systems must tell people they are dealing with a machine, deepfakes must be labelled, and AI-generated or edited content must carry machine-readable marks so it can be detected.

About a dozen AI companies were shown a finalised voluntary framework at the White House on 4 August under which developers would give the federal government access to closed frontier models 30 days before release, and the administration said it does not plan to publish the framework.

The World Bank released World Development Report 2026: The Promise of Artificial Intelligence on 4 August, reporting that 4.5 per cent of jobs in developing economies are exposed to automation by generative AI against 14.2 per cent in high income countries, and that nearly a third of rural schools in Sub-Saharan Africa still lack reliable electricity.

The Senate's science and technology committee held a public hearing on 4 August on a bill to regulate data centres, at which the Anace cacique Roberto Anace described them as a new colonisation, the Consumer Defence Institute warned that round the clock demand raises electricity costs for everyone, and a researcher from INESC said the environmental burden stays in the country while the services are exported.

Reuters reported on 6 August that the Andhra Pradesh High Court has told the state government to answer a challenge to the 15 billion US dollar Google and Adani data centre hub at Visakhapatnam, where the Kambalakonda wildlife sanctuary sits 860 metres from the site and the city draws 410 million litres of water a day against a requirement of 480 million.

Prism reported on 5 August that the Seminole Nation has approved a moratorium on AI data centre development, the Cherokee Nation has set up a task force following an executive order signed by Principal Chief Chuck Hoskin Jr in February, and the Northwestern Band of the Shoshone Nation is holding tribal councils on a proposed 10,000 acre site in Utah.

The Vanuatu Daily Post reported on 4 August that Forum ICT ministers meeting in Port Moresby on 24 July adopted the Digital Technologies and AI Principles for the Pacific, and that Vanuatu asked for protection of Pacific cultural and traditional knowledge from use in AI systems without free, prior and informed consent to be made an enforceable requirement rather than a voluntary principle in the governance framework still to be written.

President Claudia Sheinbaum told her morning press conference on 10 August that she was struck to learn young people use artificial intelligence as a psychologist, and said regional forums with parents, teachers and specialists, starting 19 August in Nuevo Leon, will produce a bill to Congress on children's use of digital platforms and AI.
The Senate Commerce Committee voted on 5 August to advance the CHATBOT Act, a bill by Ted Cruz and Brian Schatz that would give parents controls over how their children interact with AI companions.

Town commissioners voted unanimously on 3 August for a twelve month freeze on data centres after a public hearing at which residents objected on environmental grounds and over rising energy bills, and the mayor said the pause is for gathering information rather than a decision against any future facility.

Public participation on the draft Artificial Intelligence and Other Emerging Technologies Policy closed on 4 August, the deadline set when the ministry opened it on 27 July, and the draft proposes a National AI and Other Emerging Technologies Council with a governing board, a technical advisory forum and five directorates.

TechAfrica News reported on 6 August that Eduardo Mondlane University in Maputo has opened a solar powered data centre for research, cybersecurity and AI work, and that the Minister of Communications and Digital Transformation, Americo Muchanga, asked universities to take over management of the national research and education network.
Left out under the defence rule: a daily governance digest for 5 August carried an item on AI use in the Ukraine conflict.

Dropped as older than it looked: Papua New Guinea's drafting of AI deepfake offences was announced on 7 July, the UAE Federal Authority for Artificial Intelligence and Data was created on 14 June, and the Cyberspace Administration of China's draft cyberbullying law covering AI-generated abuse was published in July, all outside the seven-day regional window.

Dropped as unverified: an aggregator reported that California's Frontier AI Safety Act passed a final Assembly vote on 10 August, which no primary or legislative source confirmed, and a legislative tracker dated 7 August still had the state's AI bills at committee stage with appropriations votes set for 13 August.

Forum Foreign Ministers backed the Pacific Digital and Artificial Intelligence Technology Principles on 14 August for consideration by Forum Leaders at the 55th Pacific Islands Forum Leaders Meeting in Palau, supported a regional AI Governance Framework whose principles are to be tested and adapted before Leaders consider them in 2027, and endorsed a phased Pacific Regional Approach to Safer Digital Spaces covering shared policy principles, engagement with digital platforms and capacity building.

The Mercer County Fiscal Court passed a one year moratorium on data centre applications in unincorporated parts of the county on 11 August, and the neighbouring city of Burgin can still annex land for a hyperscale project and bypass it, which more than a dozen residents objected to on the grounds of lost farmland and lost citizen voice.

Village residents voted no on 11 August in a referendum asking whether Wrightstown should support or help build municipal infrastructure for large scale data centre development, after concerns about traffic, noise, power use and the character of the village.

El Manana de Nuevo Laredo reported on 12 August that a Texas House committee will meet in Austin on 19 August to consider whether special rules are needed to protect residents' water and electricity from data centre demand, that the Laredo representative Richard Pena Raymond has asked the Governor for a special session and a moratorium on further approvals until impacts are assessed, and that data centres in Texas do not report how much water they use and need no permit from the state environmental commission to draw groundwater.

Dropped as unverified: aggregators reported that the UK AI Regulation and Safety Bill cleared the House of Commons on 14 August, giving the AI Safety Institute statutory powers to inspect foundation models before deployment. The parliamentary bills page returned 403 and no primary or press source confirmed it. The same aggregator pattern produced a false California claim on the 11 August run.

Dropped as older than the window: Cape Town's approval of two hyperscale data centres totalling about 174MW, and the Equinix approval made despite community objections and Housing Assembly protests, were reported on 24 July and 4 August.

The Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa opened a four day stakeholder consultation in Kigali on 6 August to draft a COMESA Regional Artificial Intelligence Strategy and a Regional Digital Inclusion Strategy, with government officials, regulators, private sector, academia, civil society and development partners from member states taking part and World Bank support through its IDEA programme.

Hundreds of people marched in West Footscray in Melbourne on 9 August, from Hansen Reserve to the proposed Perri data centre site and the operating NEXTDC M3 facility, calling for a moratorium on building AI data centres and raising concerns about water supply and environmental risk, in a protest called by the Borderlands Cooperative and Citizens of Tottenham.

The Louisiana Public Service Commission voted three to one on 12 August to overturn its own administrative judge's order that Meta show how it calculated the job and electricity figures for its Hyperion data centre campus in Richland Parish, leaving those workings confidential after Meta argued they are trade secrets.

Fort Worth City Council voted unanimously on 11 August to take the first step toward a 90 day moratorium on data centre construction and to set up a Data Center and Infrastructure Committee, with city staff to use the pause to assess noise, local water supplies, long term water availability and compatibility with surrounding land uses.

Charlestown Town Council voted five to nil on 11 August to prohibit data centres and battery energy storage systems in the town, the second Rhode Island town to do so, with councillors citing the town's complete dependence on well water and septic systems and the risk of groundwater contamination.

An English language aggregator reported on 14 August that Vietnam's Ministry of Science and Technology issued a binding directive on 13 August barring government bodies from uploading classified documents to public AI platforms. A Vietnamese language source identifies the instrument as Official Dispatch 4920/BKHCN-CNCNTT dated 7 July 2026, so the item is dropped as older than it looked.

Council votes on data centre moratoria in Pima County Arizona, Bellevue Wisconsin, Waxhaw North Carolina and Marietta Georgia all fell on 11 to 13 August. The three United States items above were chosen because each turns on a different question, and the rest are the same vote repeated.

The Alberta Court of King's Bench ruled on 13 August that O'Leary Digital cannot take part in the Sturgeon Lake Cree Nation's judicial review of water licences for the C$70 billion Wonder Valley AI data centre, with Justice P. K. Johal finding the company's connection to the licence contingent and speculative, and the review of whether the Nation was consulted before Alberta granted rights to six million cubic metres from the Smoky River is set down for December.

Louisville Metro Council voted 24 to one on the night of 13 August for a six month pause on new data centre construction, or until the council approves comprehensive zoning rules, amended during the meeting to cover the conversion of existing buildings, after a developer filed to turn a 350,000 square foot warehouse in the south west of the city into a data centre; resident groups had asked for a year.

The Texas Tribune reported on 14 August that Governor Greg Abbott's 3 August order for an ERCOT audit of data centres seeking grid connections, which pauses new connection approvals while it runs, still does not say how long the audit or the pause will last or how many facilities it covers, that ERCOT expects it to take several months and to begin on 20 August, and that 43 companies including Meta, OpenAI, Microsoft and Amazon Web Services have publicly endorsed it.

Spain's Ministry of Labour and Social Economy closed a public consultation on 14 August, opened on 31 July, on a draft organic law covering generative AI in the employment of performing, audiovisual and music artists and their technical staff, which would require explicit consent and separate payment when a person's image or voice is used beyond the contracted work.

Africa AI News reported on 14 August that the Minister of ICT, Postal and Courier Services, Tatenda Mavetera, said Zimbabwe is preparing a Digital Industrial One Stop Policy covering digital transformation, cybersecurity and AI adoption, alongside a National Digital Regulatory Committee on AI regulation, data governance and digital trust and an AI Strategy Implementation Office inside the ministry.

Africa AI News reported on 14 August that the Ugandan government is consolidating more than 700 separate ICT systems covering about 350 processes into one estate to support its National Artificial Intelligence Governance Framework across 14 priority sectors including health, agriculture, banking and the judiciary.

The Arab Labour Organization, a specialised agency of the League of Arab States, held a national symposium in Egypt on 9 and 10 August with about 50 participants including the Federation of Egyptian Industries, closing with seven recommendations that included a national data governance framework, a national AI strategy tied to economic priorities, and keeping human accountability in institutional decisions that use AI.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Independence Day address from the Red Fort on 15 August was live translated into 22 Indian languages by Bhashini, the government's open source translation platform, and he pledged artificial intelligence skills training for ten million young people over the coming year under the theme Yuva Shakti for Viksit Bharat@2047.

Vietnam's Ministry of Justice announced on 14 August that it will host the ASEAN Law Forum 2026 in Hanoi on 18 and 19 August on applying artificial intelligence to law making and law enforcement, with about 150 delegates from all ASEAN member states plus Japan, South Korea, China, the UNDP, UNICEF and the OECD, and sessions on the legal frameworks member states have built for AI.

Anthropic published its second company wide Risk Report on 14 August, covering 24 February to 15 July, raising its rating of the risk of catastrophic harm from misalignment in high stakes settings from very low to low, describing the change as an uncertainty adjustment rather than a new finding, and disclosing an unreleased internal model it calls Model 2 which it says is somewhat more capable than its frontier model and which it has no current plans to release.

California's Senate and Assembly Appropriations committees held their suspense file votes on 13 August, sending on bills covering chatbots and children's safety, customer service chatbots, workplace surveillance, artificial intelligence in healthcare and student privacy, while holding AB 412 on copyright documentation requirements and AB 2545 on assessing the effect of AI on the workforce.

body: United States, Northern District of California
text: Judge William Orrick issued an order on 12 August granting in part and denying in part motions to dismiss in Andersen v Stability AI, letting the artists' direct and induced copyright infringement claims proceed to discovery, and citing a statement by Stability's chief executive that the company compressed 100,000 gigabytes of images into a two gigabyte file able to recreate any of them; trial is set for 8 September.

The Alberta government announced on 11 August four town halls on artificial intelligence data centres hosted by Technology Minister Nate Glubish, the first in Ponoka on 19 August and the second in Sturgeon County on 20 August, and Ben Baril, who plans to protest at the Sturgeon County session near Meta's proposed one gigawatt facility, said genuine consultation would have come before the projects were approved rather than after.

The Indianapolis City-County Council voted 23 to one on 10 August to stop new data centre permitting until at least 31 December 2027 so a committee of experts and residents can study campus size, building height, sound levels and environmental effects, and the three projects that drew the most community opposition, in Warren Township, Martindale-Brightwood and Decatur Township, are exempt because they are already approved.

The Fort Peck Tribal Executive Board voted on 10 August to end all future discussions between the tribal government and data centre developers across the two million acre reservation in Montana, with Chairman Floyd Azure saying three companies had approached the tribes in the past year and none could answer what benefit the tribes would get, and board member Roxanne Gourneau citing the reservation's history of contaminated drinking water.

Dropped as older than the seven day window: the Cherokee Nation banned hyperscale data centres on tribal land after a task force survey of 1,593 citizens found 64 per cent opposed, and now requires robust consultation for proposals on non tribal land inside the reservation. The decision was taken on 5 August and only reached wider outlets between 10 and 12 August.

Dropped as older than the window: INTERPOL's African Cyberthreat Assessment 2026, released on 3 August, drew on survey data from 36 African member countries and found artificial intelligence linked to 55 per cent of reported cyber incidents on the continent, with losses rising from 192 million to 484 million United States dollars since 2024.

Dropped as older than the window: President Claudia Sheinbaum announced regional forums to build a proposal for regulating artificial intelligence and social media use by children and adolescents, the first in Nuevo Leon on 19 August, then Chiapas on 3 September and Guerrero on 17 September, with the result to go to Congress. The announcement was made on 20 July, so it sits well outside the window even though the forums fall inside it.

Dropped again as older than it looked: an English language aggregator carried Vietnam's directive barring government bodies from putting classified documents into public AI platforms as dated 13 August. The instrument is Official Dispatch 4920/BKHCN-CNCNTT, dated 7 July. This is the fourth run in ten days on which an aggregator carried a date the primary source did not support.

The Pacific Islands Forum Secretariat published the outcomes of the 2026 Forum Foreign Ministers Meeting on 12 August, recording that ministers, who met in Suva on 7 August under a Solomon Islands chair, backed the Pacific Digital and Artificial Intelligence Technology Principles for Forum Leaders to consider at their 55th meeting in Palau, supported work on a regional AI Governance Framework to go to Leaders in 2027, and supported a Pacific Regional Approach to Safer Digital Spaces.

Kenya's Office of the Data Protection Commissioner closed its public consultation on 17 August on three draft guidance notes covering artificial intelligence, emerging technologies and privacy-enhancing technologies, with the AI note mapping the Data Protection Act onto each stage of an AI system's life and placing content recommendation engines in the same compliance bracket as facial recognition and loan scoring.

Brazil's national data protection authority closed a public consultation on 17 August, open since 30 June on the government's Brasil Participativo platform, on rules for digital platforms under Decree 12,976 of 2026, which requires platforms to take down non-consensual intimate images within two hours of notice and bars the use of artificial intelligence to create false intimate images.

Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif chaired a meeting on 16 August reviewing progress on Punjab AI Vision 2029, a six-pillar plan she said should make Punjab the most artificial intelligence enabled province in South Asia by 2029, and directed work on an AI-enabled delivery unit and a Chief Minister AI stocktake to monitor it.

Crusoe's Project Flash data centre at Summit View Business Park in Franklin County, Virginia was dropped on 17 August after strained negotiations and opposition from residents, more than 200 of whom had attended meetings raising concerns about transparency and further development.

ROI-NJ reported on 17 August that Bayonne, New Jersey has banned data centres, with the city council approving the prohibition unanimously on 13 August and Mayor Sharon Ashe-Nadrowski signing it after months of grassroots opposition.

Residents of Granbury, Texas asked a Fort Worth appeals court on 17 August to revive a recall effort against the mayor and four council members over their handling of the Project Patriot data centre, alleging breaches of open meeting rules in how the zoning approval was made.

Colorado's House Bill 26-1263, which requires operators of conversational artificial intelligence services to disclose that the service is not a person, run a self-harm response protocol and estimate user age, entered into force on 12 August, with its content moderation duties for minors following on 1 January 2027.

The ASEAN Law Forum 2026 opened in Hanoi on 18 August on applying artificial intelligence to law making and law enforcement, with Deputy Prime Minister Le Tien Chau proposing four areas of cooperation: common principles for AI in lawmaking and enforcement, shared standards for digitising legal data, training people who hold both legal and technical skills, and a standing dialogue between member states for sharing experience.

Lesotho's Ministry of Information, Communications, Science, Technology and Innovation opened a five day workshop with the United Nations in Maseru on 17 August to draft a National AI Strategy and a Data Centre Blueprint, with Deputy Prime Minister Justice Nthomeng Majara calling for safeguards, policies and human capacity to be in place before AI investment is scaled up, and Minister Nthati Moorosi saying more than 100 stakeholders validated related policies in 2025.

Dubuque published the results of its data centre survey on 18 August: of 3,777 responses, 76 per cent said they would not support a data centre and more than 90 per cent named energy use, water use and environmental effects as the most important things for an ordinance to cover, with the council due to vote on a six month moratorium on 8 September, a draft ordinance in November and a final vote expected in December.

Westover City Council in Alabama voted unanimously on 18 August for a six month moratorium on data centres, having tabled the ordinance at its previous meeting, after residents objected to a proposed development during public comment, with Mayor Bobby Pardue saying the pause gives the city time to make the changes it needs.

The Louisiana Public Service Commission voted on 12 August to cancel a subpoena that would have required Meta to disclose its investment, its permanent job numbers and the electricity its north Louisiana data centre will demand, overruling the administrative law judge who had ordered the disclosure, after an hour and a half of public testimony from more than 20 people and objections from the Union of Concerned Scientists, the Alliance for Affordable Energy and Earthjustice; the commission decides on the associated gas plants on 16 December.

Government News published criticism on 19 August of the Office of AI set up inside the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet, with technologist Lambros Photios arguing that spreading responsibility for the national framework across several ministers leaves no single minister accountable for it.

Cybersecurity specialist Alex Teh told the annual Fiji CyberSec conference on 18 August that criminals are using artificial intelligence to run phishing and deepfake attacks at greater speed and scale, that the Pacific has become a cyber frontline as connectivity grows, and that the roughly 1,000 IT graduates Fiji produces each year are a workforce the country could build a cybersecurity capability on.

Governor Josh Shapiro signed Executive Order 2026-05 on 18 August, directing the Department of Environmental Protection to review a data centre permit application only where the developer has made a legally binding commitment to the Governor's Responsible Infrastructure Development requirements and has already received local approval, removing AI data centre proposals from the state's fast track permitting process and prohibiting non-disclosure agreements on data centre projects, after the state House passed the same requirements and the Senate declined to bring them to a vote.

Chesapeake City Council voted unanimously on 19 August for a data centre zoning ordinance that allows new facilities only as a conditional use in industrial areas, prohibits them from drawing groundwater, and closes the by right development route that had let projects proceed without a council decision.

Keller City Council voted unanimously on 19 August to take legal action against the neighbouring town of Westlake over a proposed 1.1 million square foot data centre on their shared boundary, and began a 90 day moratorium process of its own, a case of one town taking its neighbour to court over a development on their shared boundary.

Vietnam's Ministry of Science and Technology issued a binding directive on 13 August prohibiting government agencies from uploading classified documents to public artificial intelligence platforms, which techtimes.com describes as the first time a Southeast Asian country has turned its AI law into an operational enforcement instruction.

Mozambique's information and communication technologies institute INTIC held a national and inclusive dialogue on 14 August on artificial intelligence and the cultural and creative economy, with the discussion centred on ethical governance, algorithmic transparency and protecting intellectual property in AI generated content, following its presentation of a draft national AI strategy to Vodacom on 12 August.

The first of Mexico's regional forums on regulating children's use of digital platforms, social media and artificial intelligence opened on 19 August at the Universidad Autonoma de Nuevo Leon in Monterrey, two days after President Claudia Sheinbaum announced that more than a million basic education teachers would be asked their view on regulating phones in schools during the school technical council sessions on 24 and 25 August, with the forums' conclusions to be sent to the Congress of the Union to support a possible bill.

New South Wales released a Data Centre Policy Framework on 17 August, which pv-tech.org describes as the first state translation of Australia's national data centre policy direction into operating rules, requiring data centres to be net generators of renewable energy rather than net consumers, putting the cost of the extra energy infrastructure on the centres rather than on households and small businesses, ordering an independent review of water pricing to protect water security for other communities, and offering a 75 day assessment commitment to developers that meet the performance measures.

Nye County commissioners voted five to nil on 18 August to ban data centres in Basin 162, the Pahrump Valley groundwater basin, then voted four to one to set a public hearing on land use rules, special use permits and development standards for data centres in the rest of the county, while a third item proposing a special election on the question received no motion and failed.

District Court Judge Frank Joseph declined on 19 August to rule immediately in the lawsuit brought by the group 406 People First against the county clerk over 3,652 signatures rejected on 10 August for a ballot initiative that would let Butte residents vote on whether data centres are allowed in the county, and ordered further briefing before deciding the following week.

At a seminar on artificial intelligence cooperation with China reported on 17 August, SMART Zambia national coordinator Percy Chinyama warned against adopting models built for mature environments without regard to Zambian circumstances, capabilities and culture, and Ministry of Technology and Science permanent secretary Dr Brilliant Habeenzu said cooperation should build on existing national capabilities rather than substitute for them, with officials citing Zambia's retained ownership of the health data in its SmartCare Pro platform as the precedent.

Ghana opened its 2026 National ICT Week on 17 August with deputy minister Mohammed Adam Sukparu describing the national artificial intelligence strategy adopted in April 2026 as covering data governance, infrastructure, talent development, ethical use and practical applications, and pointing to an AI capacity building programme for public officials run with UNESCO, the UN Development Programme and Japan.

A St Joseph County vote to widen a tax increment financing district to take in a Microsoft data centre project, expected in the week after 19 August, was moved to 22 September, with councilwoman Amy Drake questioning how the tax revenue would be shared rather than returned to taxpayers, and council candidate Jan Cervelli running a public education session to explain what the financing district would mean.
Left out under the defence rule: the National Information Technology Development Agency urged the Nigerian Army on 20 August to use artificial intelligence and data for modern warfare.

text: Chile's Ministry of Science set six axes for 2026 to 2030 and said a new artificial intelligence bill would replace the one in its second reading in the Senate, but that was 13 August. Parliamentarians from sixteen Asia-Pacific countries, including Samoa, Fiji, Vanuatu, Papua New Guinea and Tonga, called for responsible AI at a forum in Phnom Penh on 11 to 13 August. The World Bank's World Development Report 2026 on artificial intelligence, which reached African coverage on 17 August, was launched on 4 August. The Brazilian Senate's science and technology committee hearing on regulating AI data centres was 4 August. The British government's concession in the Iver data centre judicial review was January 2026.

Six other American local data centre items surfaced on 20 August: Google confirmed as the end user of a 506 acre campus in Tulsa County, a planning subcommittee formed in Bay City, a 45 day moratorium approved in Tulare County, citizen petitions gathered in Piedmont, rules under consideration in Austin, and the mayor of Sioux Falls arguing against a moratorium. Logging them would have made the page mostly American local government again.

Vietnam's list of 46 high-risk artificial intelligence systems took effect on 15 August under Decision 33/2026/QD-TTg, covering transport with 31 systems, ethnicity and religion with seven, education with three, healthcare and banking with two each and litigation with one, and requiring providers to report the risk level to the Ministry of Science and Technology before use, run a conformity assessment and keep a risk management plan running for the life of the system.

Nigeria's National Information Technology Development Agency and the Budget Office of the Federation inaugurated a Joint Technical Committee on the National Sovereign Cloud Initiative on 21 August, chaired by Budget Office director general Tanimu Yakubu with NITDA director general Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi as co-chair, to work through the government cloud spending, procurement, financing, connectivity, power, cybersecurity and data governance questions the initiative raises.

The GSMA released a report in Lilongwe on 20 August finding that about 80 per cent of Malawians are offline although 87 per cent live under 4G coverage, with unique mobile internet penetration at 12.5 per cent and smartphone adoption at 33 per cent, and recommending Malawi develop a national artificial intelligence strategy aligned with wider African frameworks alongside a coordinated national digital economy strategy.

Pope Leo XIV told the International Catholic Legislators Network at the Vatican on 21 August, during its meeting in Rome from 20 to 23 August, that legislation on emerging technologies should protect users from exploitation, preserve personal privacy, require transparency in how the technologies are used and guarantee that they strengthen democratic institutions.

The Texas House Committee on State Affairs sat for more than six hours on 19 August taking invited and public testimony on data centre development and on the planning process behind proposed 765 kilovolt transmission lines, with the chair capping data centre testimony at 2pm to make room for the transmission item, water experts and local officials among those heard, and ERCOT chief executive Pablo Vegas telling members the state audit of interconnection requests ordered on 3 August will not finish until late 2026.

Salix City Council voted three to two on the evening of 20 August against a one year pause on data centre development that the council could have shortened or extended, at a meeting held a week late because city officials had received death and terroristic threats on social media, and after Google was named in early August as the prospective customer for the roughly 900 acres of farmland the town annexed in April.
Nothing was excluded under the defence rule.

Dropped as older than the window: Panama's Cabinet Council adopted the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy by Resolution 89-26, but that was reported on 12 August. The Caribbean Telecommunications Union's Caribbean AI Task Force final report was launched at the Caribbean AI Forum on 23 and 24 July. The Cherokee Nation's ban on hyperscale data centres on tribal and trust land was early August and is already noted on this page. Figures circulating from a Data Centers and Energy forum in Santiago dated 21 August turned out to be from August 2025, not this year.

Held rather than logged: the American local data centre items running through 20 and 21 August were the same set already held on yesterday's entry, with Tulsa County, Bay City, Tulare County, Piedmont, Austin and Sioux Falls all still moving. Salix is logged instead because the vote went against a moratorium and because the meeting had been delayed by threats against officials.

Searched and found nothing inside the window: Latin America in Spanish and Portuguese, the Caribbean, the Middle East in Arabic and English, and the Pacific in the PACNEWS bulletins for 19, 20 and 21 August, which carried no artificial intelligence or data centre item. The Pacific Islands Forum foreign ministers' AI principles are already on this page from the 14 and 18 August scans.

The ASEAN Law Forum met in Hanoi on 18 and 19 August on applying artificial intelligence in law making and law enforcement, with justice officials from all ten member states, the ASEAN Secretariat, the Japanese Ministry of Justice, the UN Development Programme, UNICEF and the European Union taking part, and Vietnamese deputy justice minister Nguyen Thanh Tinh closing on 19 August by saying the countries shared an understanding that artificial intelligence must be grounded in the rule of law, transparency and accountability, that no single governance model suits every country, and that the forum's ideas should be turned into regional cooperation frameworks.

Chesapeake City Council voted nine to nil on 18 August to take data centres off the by right track altogether, so every future project needs a conditional use permit, and the ordinance also bars data centres from connecting to groundwater, after a hearing at which close to forty people spoke and most of them opposed data centres in the city at all; an eight month pause on applications already in place means nothing can come before the council until early next year.

Harrington City Council voted unanimously on the evening of 17 August against an ordinance that would have allowed data centres as a conditional use in the city's manufacturing zones, after close to an hour of public comment from a crowd of about a hundred people that filled a library meeting room and spilled into the hallway, with residents raising water, sewer capacity, electricity, infrastructure and noise; the decision blocks a 24 megawatt project on the former Harrington Logistics site.

El Paso County Commissioners Court approved a resolution on 17 August and wrote to Governor Greg Abbott asking whether the data centre protections he ordered on 3 August reach the borderland at all, since El Paso sits outside the ERCOT grid those protections were built around, and asking him to pause further data centre development until water use, electricity costs, infrastructure and environmental impacts are dealt with, and to consider calling a special session of the legislature.

Fairborn City Council passed a resolution on 21 August setting a twelve month pause on new data centres, and on self storage, convenience stores, service stations and car washes with them, with members saying the city has little commercial and industrial land left and that decisions about how it is used will shape the town for decades.

A Vietnamese delegation led by ambassador Bui Van Nghi visited Porto Alegre in Rio Grande do Sul from 17 to 19 August to widen cooperation on semiconductors, artificial intelligence and digital transformation, and the embassy and the Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul jointly ran a Vietnam and Latin America forum on innovation and digital transformation there on 19 August, which took up Vietnam's place in the Global South, the effect of artificial intelligence on education and workforce development, and the use of large data sets in precision agriculture.

Five more American local items fell inside the window and were left off to stop the page becoming almost entirely American: a one year moratorium passed five to nil in Alamance County, North Carolina on 17 August; Keller, Texas voting unanimously on 19 August to take legal action against neighbouring Westlake over a data centre proposed 506 feet from homes; a four month pause in Spokane County, Washington; a one year pause in Kalamazoo, Michigan; and a court action filed on 17 August in Granbury, Texas to revive a recall of the mayor and four council members.

text: Thailand's Board of Investment four test screening framework for data centres was announced on 10 August. Statesboro, Georgia approved a data centre rezoning three to two on 18 August and sits with the held American items.

text: No defence or military item was dropped from this scan.

The federal government expects to settle mandatory national standards for large artificial intelligence data centres at a national cabinet meeting on Wednesday 26 August, the ABC reported on 24 August, with the rules requiring big centres to draw their power from new renewable projects and to underwrite their own energy and water infrastructure, Queensland and the Northern Territory saying they will not sign a standard that rules out coal and gas, energy minister Chris Bowen saying the government wants data centre investment that is in the best interest of Australians, Queensland premier David Crisafulli framing his objection as data sovereignty and respect for communities' wishes, and the Commonwealth signalling it will legislate the causer pays energy rules next year whether or not every state and territory agrees.

The Andhra Pradesh government approved AM AI Factory (Vizag) Pvt Ltd on Saturday 22 August to build a 512 megawatt green integrated artificial intelligence data centre at Amanam village in Bheemunipatnam mandal in Visakhapatnam district, an investment of more than 31,387 crore rupees expected to employ up to 1,000 people and to be built within two years and four months, with the state providing power infrastructure support and undertaking to ensure water supply, alongside exemptions from stamp duty and electricity duty.

President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva launched about 444 million United States dollars of artificial intelligence spending at a ceremony in Rio Grande do Norte on 20 August, splitting the work between a 1.3 billion real supercomputer in Rio de Janeiro built with the Chinese firms Huawei and iFlytek and a tender of about 1 billion reais in the north east expected to go to the American chipmaker Nvidia, with the government saying the strategy is not to depend on a single company, technology or country, and adding a national centre for algorithmic transparency at the Federal University of Minas Gerais and semiconductor work with Spain.

The California Senate gave SB 1159 final passage thirty seven votes to nil on 20 August, a bill that states an artificial intelligence system is not a person under the state's public records and open meeting laws.

Amnesty International published a report on 18 August finding that Argentina spent about 1.2 million United States dollars on artificial intelligence surveillance tools across 2024 and 2025, including facial recognition, social media monitoring and aerial surveillance, drawing on 21 interviews with journalists, activists and human rights defenders alongside procurement documents and freedom of information requests, and asking the government to prohibit remote biometric recognition used for discriminatory surveillance and to put accountability mechanisms around the rest.

Lesotho's Ministry of Information, Communications, Science, Technology and Innovation ran a five day workshop in Maseru from 17 to 21 August with the United Nations in Lesotho to draft a National AI Strategy and a Data Centre Blueprint, with deputy prime minister Justice Nthomeng Majara calling for a cautious and strategic approach that assesses the country's existing capability and puts safeguards, infrastructure, policy and people in place before scaling investment, and minister Nthati Moorosi noting that more than 100 stakeholders were brought together in 2025 to validate related policies.

Left out under the defence rule: NITDA director general Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi urged the Nigerian Army on 20 August to use artificial intelligence and data for modern warfare, which is a military application and outside this page's scope.

text: Vanuatu's call for Pacific cultural and traditional knowledge to be protected from artificial intelligence systems without free, prior and informed consent, and for that safeguard to be enforceable rather than voluntary, was delivered by special envoy Fred Samuel at the Forum ICT Ministers Meeting in Port Moresby that closed on 23 July and was reported on 4 August. Chile's science ministry said on 13 August it will bring a new artificial intelligence bill to replace the one in its second reading in the Senate. The Abidjan Declaration 2026 to 2030, adopted by data protection authorities from 24 African countries, was May 2026. Palm Beach County's refusal of the Project Tango data centre resurfaced in Spanish language coverage on 19 August but the vote itself was July.

The Andhra Pradesh High Court heard the public interest petition against the Google and Adani data centre hub near the Kambalakonda wildlife sanctuary and the Mudasarlova drinking water reservoir in Visakhapatnam on 24 August, with counsel for the state telling the bench that care and caution is being exercised in ensuring that all steps are taken within the parameters of law, the petitioner arguing that temple land is involved, that no environmental impact study was done, and that the project sits close to forest and water reservoirs in a city already short of water, and the court giving the state and its authorities until a hearing next week to file counter affidavits.

The Chamber of Deputies science, technology and innovation committee approved Bill 4356/25 on 20 August, which sets rules for artificial intelligence used in Brazil's unified public security system and requires human supervision of every action and decision an artificial intelligence system produces, barring automatic arrests and seizures without qualified human intervention, with deputy Coronel Meira as rapporteur, and the proposal now going to three further committees before the Chamber and the Senate can pass it.

A presidential circular published in the Official Gazette on 18 August put the Türkiye Artificial Intelligence Action Plan 2026 to 2030 into force, coordinated by the Ministry of Industry and Technology and following the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy that ran from 2021 to 2025, with technological sovereignty, data driven development, public sector efficiency and international competitiveness set as its aims, and human centredness, reliability, ethical responsibility, digital sovereignty and sustainable development named as its guiding principles.

The Cabinet Office put a revised draft Principle Code on protecting intellectual property and ensuring transparency in generative artificial intelligence to the thirteenth meeting of its study group on intellectual property rights in the artificial intelligence era on 18 August, resting on three pillars: publishing an overview of models, training data and accountability measures, answering enquiries from rights holders who are pursuing legal proceedings, and answering enquiries from users who generated content with the service, with no legal force behind it and a comply or explain approach taken from corporate governance stewardship codes.

The Australian Parliament appointed a Joint Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence on 20 August, with the government backing an opposition initiative, to examine the effect of artificial intelligence on national security, productivity, competitiveness and living standards, and to look at whether existing laws are adequate, at the importance of data sovereignty, and at the impact on communities.

The Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa opened a four day stakeholder consultation in Lilongwe, reported on 21 August, drawing on the public sector, the private sector, academia, development partners and civil society to build a regional artificial intelligence and digital inclusion strategy, an action plan and model policies, with COMESA infrastructure and logistics director Bernard Dzawanda saying artificial intelligence can transform public service delivery, agriculture, healthcare and trade but also raises governance and ethical questions that need coordinated regional responses, and Malawi's information and communications technology minister Shadric Namalomba saying digital transformation will benefit the region only when all citizens have equitable access to digital technologies.

Left out under the defence rule: the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy released a National Security Science and Technology Strategy on 18 August that puts artificial intelligence and autonomous systems at the front of military capability, which is a defence item and outside this page's scope.

Dropped as older than it looked: an aggregator dated the National Cyber Security Centre's warning about frontier models taking unsanctioned actions to 20 August, but the NCSC's own statement is dated 4 August, so it was not logged.

Dropped as older than the window: CARICOM's agreement to set up a regional Blue Ribbon Commission on Artificial Intelligence at its summit in Gros Islet, Saint Lucia was reported on 3 August; Amazon Web Services withdrew its Calvert Cliffs data centre application in Maryland on 4 August; Malaysia's public consultation on its AI Governance Bill closed on 31 July; Kenya's draft artificial intelligence and emerging technologies policy closed for submissions on 4 August; the joint comments by the Electronic Frontier Foundation, Public Knowledge and Fight for the Future against the Federal Trade Commission's artificial intelligence policy proposal were 3 August; and the Canadian civil society open letter opposing the National Sprint consultation was October 2025.

National Cabinet met the Prime Minister in Sydney this morning with the proposed mandatory standards for large artificial intelligence data centres on the agenda, and the ABC reported at 5:15am that New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory back the standards while Queensland and the Northern Territory still object, energy minister Chris Bowen saying the government is requiring new data centres to bring their own renewable energy backed by gas firming and repeating that the Commonwealth is prepared to legislate over the states, Queensland deputy premier Jarrod Bleijie replying that Bowen should be working with state and territory governments rather than acting as a big brother bully, and the report putting data centre electricity use on a path from 3 per cent of national supply to 13 per cent within a decade. This page recorded on 24 August that the meeting was expected to settle the standards; what is new is the line up of states, the projected share of the grid, and that the meeting is under way. The outcome was not known at the time of this scan.

The New Mexico Supreme Court unanimously granted two petitions from environmental groups late on Sunday 23 August, pausing the state Environment Department's air quality permit hearing for the natural gas fuel cell system proposed at Project Jupiter, the Oracle and OpenAI data centre campus under construction in Doña Ana County, and ordering the Office of the State Engineer to stop allowing water from a particular well to be used for the site's construction, with both orders answering arguments that the permitting processes denied the groups due process, the air hearing that had been set for 14 September in Sunland Park now off the calendar, and the hearing officer in that case standing aside.

The substance of the 24 August hearing logged here yesterday has since been reported: the bench headed by Chief Justice Lisa Gill declined the petitioner's request for an interim status quo, which would have stopped work at the site, and instead directed the state to ensure that construction of the Google and Adani data centre project in Visakhapatnam goes ahead only after every legal and environmental permission is obtained, with a consolidated response required from the departments that granted the approvals before the matter returns next week.

The Planning and Zoning Commission of Ozark voted unanimously on 25 August to recommend a data centre code to the Board of Aldermen, which would allow micro and large load data centres only on land zoned industrial and only with a conditional use permit and a public hearing, and would require an environmental impact report, disclosure of the building's size and intended use, compliance with noise limits, and a prohibition on open loop and once through cooling, with the city saying it has received no application from any developer.

body: Spartanburg County, South Carolina, United States
text: The Lightstone Group's proposed 200,000 square foot, 60 megawatt data centre at 300 Jones Road went to the county Board of Zoning Appeals on 25 August after county staff denied the application in June for not complying with the land management ordinance and rejected a revised submission in July on procedural grounds, with the county's proposed one year pause on new data centre applications still awaiting its third reading, which council put off on 17 August to hear from more residents and experts and has now listed for 21 September.

A third listed California's SB 947, the No Robo Bosses Act, on 25 August, but the state Senate passed it 29 votes to 9 on 20 May.

Pacific Islands Forum foreign ministers backed the Pacific Digital and Artificial Intelligence Technology Principles on 14 August, for Forum Leaders to consider in Palau from 30 August. National Cabinet agreed on 26 August that large data centres have material impacts on energy, water and land use and that the Commonwealth will work with the states and territories on consistent mandatory national standards covering those three areas along with skills and training, the Prime Minister saying the standards would be legislated early next year, and the proposal that new large centres underwrite additional renewable generation with gas firming did not survive into the agreement, Queensland and the Northern Territory keeping a technology agnostic approach that allows gas or coal, which the Queensland Premier called a good win for his state.

The Centre for Policy Alternatives, a Colombo policy institute, published a statement on 23 August on the government's plan to pilot artificial intelligence assisted drafting of legislation, starting with the proposed Virtual Asset Service Providers Bill in Sinhala, Tamil and English, saying that lawmaking in the country already suffers from inadequate consultation and limited transparency, warning that political choices presented as objective machine output would let decision makers step away from accountability, and asking for mandatory human review, public disclosure whenever the tools are used, independent audits for bias and accuracy, data protection standards and real openings for public scrutiny.

Figures reported on 24 August show data centres drawing on Ireland's public water supply used 514 million litres between May and July, close to double the 276 million litres they used over the four months from January to April, with July alone above 200 million litres, about what 50,000 people use, and Uisce Eireann, the national water utility, said the volume is a fraction of total production and not a risk to public supply, while the government's data centre report replaced a draft recommendation for measurable targets on water use with a call for transparent reporting on energy and water instead.

body: Durham County, North Carolina, United States
text: Durham County commissioners voted four to one on Monday 24 August for a nine month pause on new large data centres, running to May 2027 and matching the pause the city of Durham had already adopted, with the ordinance exempting only buildings under 100,000 square feet that use closed loop cooling and no diesel backup generators, which leaves the hyperscale projects covered, residents having raised water use, electricity demand, noise and air and water pollution, and the one commissioner who voted against saying she opposed the exemption rather than the pause.

The Marshalltown city council passed the second and third readings of a four month pause on data centre applications on 25 August, in force from 27 August to 23 November, with residents asking that the people who pay the rates be the ones to decide and that the wider community be drawn into the conversation, and the developer Swarm Systems telling the council it wanted the chance to meet whatever standards the city sets, putting its proposal at about 345 million United States dollars, roughly 3 million a year in property tax and 50 to 60 permanent jobs, with no tax incentive sought.

text: A data centre digest dated 25 August listed three moratorium decisions that had happened earlier: Madison County in Arkansas passed its three year pause on 17 August, Westover in Alabama passed its six month pause on 18 August, and the Westover town hall was on 20 August. A search result dated 24 August on Mexico turned on President Claudia Sheinbaum's remark that the country will not become the world's data centre, which she made at her morning press conference on 18 August.

Searches by name for Africa, Latin America, the Caribbean, the Middle East, Central Asia, the Pacific beyond Australia and East and South East Asia, including searches in Spanish, Portuguese, French and Arabic, returned nothing inside the seven day window that is not already on this page. Standing items outside the window: the Pacific Islands Forum leaders meet in Palau from 30 August with the Pacific Digital and Artificial Intelligence Technology Principles before them, the House of Lords inquiry into the United Kingdom's Online Safety Act takes written evidence until 7 September, and Japan's revised guidelines for government procurement and use of generative artificial intelligence take effect on 1 September.

The Ministry for the Ecological Transition opened a public consultation on 27 August on a draft royal decree covering the energy sustainability, environmental protection, resilience and digital sovereignty of data centres, which would apply to new sites drawing a megawatt or more, set interim efficiency thresholds of 1.15 for power use and 0.1 for water use until the European classification system starts in August 2027, require a substantial share of the electricity consumed to be matched by newly built renewable generation, and require operators to be based in the European Union with public sector data held and moved only inside it, with companies, organisations and any other interested party able to file observations until 4 September.

The Green Party of England and Wales called on 28 August for a pause on approvals for new large scale data centres in England, its leader Zack Polanski telling the BBC that the government is putting artificial intelligence companies ahead of water stressed communities after the driest July on record, with the party's objection resting on the classification of data centres as critical national infrastructure, which places them alongside energy, water and food for priority access during a drought, and the party asking for an exception only for local scale centres serving a local community, while Labour rejected the call on the ground that it would cost jobs.

The Mozambican Association of Artificial Intelligence was launched in Maputo on 28 August with its leadership sworn in at a ceremony opened by Lourino Chemane, chairman of the National Institute of Information and Communication Technologies, the association bringing together government bodies, private companies, universities, researchers, technology professionals, entrepreneurs and civil society, and the institute coordinating a proposed National Artificial Intelligence Strategy and a national data governance policy alongside it.

A report published on 27 August set out how the water demand of data centres is being contested across South East Asia, with eighteen areas of Batam in Indonesia already classed as water scarce and household demand there projected at 280 million cubic metres a year against 139 million available, a single new centre using 3,000 cubic metres a day, about what 30,000 residents use, and nine planned centres by 2032 needing 29,000 cubic metres a day or roughly 8 per cent of the island's supply, with Batam residents protesting since December 2024 and occupying the mayor's office in January 2026, Greenpeace Malaysia and eight other civil society organisations objecting on emissions, noise, urban heat and water, Johor tightening its approval criteria to require sufficient energy and water, and Malaysia's National Water Services Commission issuing guidelines for developers.

OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services, Oracle, IBM, Hugging Face and more than a hundred other technology, finance and manufacturing companies published a joint open letter on 27 August saying that artificial intelligence enabled cyberattacks will become far more widespread within months and that the services communities depend on, from hospitals to water treatment plants to the infrastructure that carries the internet, are at risk, asking governments to coordinate locally, nationally and internationally, to fund essential services with limited budgets, and to widen access to defensive tools for hospitals, water utilities and local governments, and asking frontier artificial intelligence companies to provide funding, training and hands on support to operators who cannot act on their own.

The Eastport planning board voted unanimously on 27 August to recommend that the city adopt a permanent ban on data centres across every zoning district, widening a citizen initiated ordinance that the city's own lawyers had already found legally sound subject to formatting, the same lawyers finding a second citizen petition unlawful because it would have required a public vote on any new industrial or commercial development above 25,000 square feet on land or 10,000 square feet in the water, with the city council due to consider the recommendation on 9 September, the council having adopted a 180 day pause on 14 August, and the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission having accepted DeepGreen Western Passage's preliminary permit application on 24 August to explore placing a tidal powered data centre underwater off the city.

The Palm Springs city council voted unanimously on 26 August for a 45 day pause on new large scale data centres, running to 10 October while the city considers zoning rules over the next two years, with residents raising water use, electricity demand and the extra cooling a desert site needs, other residents asking the council to keep the door open to future development, and councilmember Grace Garner saying the city needs to be thoughtful about regulating an industry that is changing quickly because other communities have faced huge detriments, the decision following temporary pauses in Desert Hot Springs and Indio and a permanent ban approved in Coachella in the same week.

The Garfield Township board voted unanimously on Tuesday 25 August for a one year pause on data centres and cryptocurrency mining, extendable by six months, adopted as a zoning ordinance amendment recommended by the planning commission rather than as a standalone resolution, after residents packed a zoning meeting in July over water, electricity rates and the environment, which stalls a proposal by an Illinois developer to convert a building on Cass Road into a small scale data centre.

Ahead: the 55th Pacific Islands Forum Leaders Meeting sits in Palau from 30 August to 4 September with the Pacific Digital and Artificial Intelligence Technology Principles before leaders, submissions to the Australian Senate inquiry into artificial intelligence and data centres close on 1 September, Japan's revised guidelines for government procurement and use of generative artificial intelligence take effect on 1 September, Spain's data centre consultation closes on 4 September, the Eastport city council takes up the permanent ban on 9 September, Mexico's regional forums run to 17 September, and Spartanburg County in South Carolina has its third reading on a one year pause listed for 21 September.
